slot.brief: Given combination of gates feeding an output, construct truth table for all input combinations; identify equivalent single gate (NAND/NOR logic reduction).

stem: For binary inputs $A$ and $B$, where NAND denotes the usual NAND operation, define $P=\operatorname{NAND}(A,B)$, $Q=\operatorname{NAND}(A,A)$, $R=\operatorname{NAND}(B,B)$, $S=\operatorname{NAND}(Q,R)$ and $Y=\operatorname{NAND}(S,P)$. Which single gate has the same truth table as $Y$?

verdicts.working: Q=¬A and R=¬B, so S=A∨B. Since P=¬(A∧B), Y=¬[(A∨B)∧¬(A∧B)]=¬(A⊕B), which is XNOR.

working:
For $(A,B)=(00,01,10,11)$, $P=(1,1,1,0)$ and $S=(0,1,1,1)$; hence $Y=S\ \operatorname{NAND}\ P=(1,0,0,1)$, the XNOR truth table.

Independent check: Q=¬A and R=¬B, so S=A∨B. Since P=¬(A∧B), Y=¬[(A∨B)∧¬(A∧B)]=¬(A⊕B), which is XNOR.
solution:
Using NAND as negated AND, $Q=
eg A$ and $R=
eg B$, so $S=
eg(QR)=A\lor B$.
$$Y=
eg(SP)=
eg\big[(A\lor B)\land
eg(A\land B)\big]=
eg(A\oplus B)$$
Thus $Y$ has the XNOR truth table.
